title: Mutable and Immutable Data
learningObjectives: Explain the main concept in this lesson.
Identify how references, state, or lifetime affect behavior.
Trace an example and predict its result.
Choose an appropriate practice for a simple scenario.

understand.concept: Mutable data can change after creation. Immutable data cannot be changed in place under its language rules; an operation may instead produce a new value. Mutability affects shared state, testing, concurrency, and API design.
understand.whyItMatters: Immutability can reduce unexpected changes and simplify reasoning; mutability can be useful for efficient updates.
understand.analogy: A printed page stays unchanged while a whiteboard can be edited. Software rules are more precise than the analogy.
understand.analogyLimit: This analogy simplifies software rules; language and runtime behavior may differ.

explain.narrative: Identify the data or resource, who can access it, and how it changes or remains available. Trace the example, and consider what happens after a function returns or when an error interrupts normal flow. Use language-specific lifecycle and ownership rules for real implementations.

examples.title: Mutate an object

examples.title: Changed copy
examples.explanation: The spread creates a separate top-level object with a new property value.

examples.title: Freeze object
examples.explanation: Freeze is shallow and prevents property changes on this object in standard JavaScript.

commonMistakes: Confusing a constant binding with immutable data.
Assuming shallow copies duplicate nested objects.
